Latest Update: Dion Sanderson challenges damning Derby County admission as Rams struggles continue

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (510 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Derby County have been one of the surprise packages in the Championship so far this season, but for all the wrong reasons.
  • The Rams sit 23rd in the table after 16 games with just 10 points to their name, and their misery was compounded after returning from the international break with a 2-0 defeat at the hands of Southampton on Saturday.
  • Recent findings suggest that there was a sense of optimism around Pride Park ahead of the start of the new season.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Derby County have been one of the surprise packages in the Championship so far this season, but for all the wrong reasons.

The Rams sit 23rd in the table after 16 games with just 10 points to their name, and their misery was compounded after returning from the international break with a 2-0 defeat at the hands of Southampton on Saturday.

Recent findings suggest that there was a sense of optimism around Pride Park ahead of the start of the new season. After last term's excellent eighth place finish and the expansion of the play-offs, there was a real sense that Derby could finally have a crack at promotion to the Premier League.

John Eustace had worked wonders since his arrival in February 2025, building a squad that was seemingly capable of fighting at the sharp end of the Championship.

However, with just one win in 14 league matches to start the fresh season, the Rams were left cut adrift with Burnley and Preston in the relegation zone, with no escape looking likely.

A much-needed victory over Bolton Wanderers in the final game before the early November international break gave supporters hope that things could turn around, but Saturday's defeat at St Mary's was a depressing thud back down to reality.

Following Saturday's defeat at Southampton, Rams defender Dion Sanderson faced BBC Sport Derby to give his verdict on a difficult run of fixtures ahead, and it's fair to say his words will cut deep for supporters.

"Everything's different, different teams, we prepare differently each week," Sanderson mentioned.

"But I think from a personal note, it doesn't matter what team you're up against, you've got to play for the badge on your shirt, play for the club, and play for yourself, a bit of pride.

Sources indicate that "I think the lads this week, especially, have got to continue [the intensity in training]. We've got to take that onto next week and the week after.

Industry observers note that "We are in a relegation scrap and that's the reality of it. The lads need to start pulling their socks up now, and we're asking a lot from everyone," the defender concluded.

After just 16 games, a player admitting that a relegation scrap is on the cards certainly isn't what fans will want to be hearing, especially after how much optimism there was heading into the season.

After the interview with Sanderson was posted to X by BBC Sport Derby, some Rams supporters reacted to what their centre-back had to say in the wake of yet another disappointing defeat.

One fan remained surprisingly positive, suggesting Derby did enough to earn a point and encouraged the players to keep their heads up.

Another wasn't quite as forgiving, calling Sanderson 'hopeless'.

Another also voiced their frustrations at Sanderson himself, suggesting he should let his performances do the talking rather than post-match interviews.

Finally, one fan blamed club CEO Stephen Pearce for the mess the club currently finds itself in, and suggested nothing will get better until he is replaced.

#129917. Latest Update: 5 managers Watford FC must eye up ASAP after Dionisi sack ft ex-Arsenal coach

Latest Update: 5 managers Watford FC must eye up ASAP after Dionisi sack ft ex-Arsenal coach

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1246 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Continuing to struggle down at the bottom end of the Championship table, Watford have now taken the decision to sack manager Alessio Dionisi.
  • Following a 5-1 defeat to Cardiff City last month, it was reported then that Dionisi was set to be sacked by Watford, but he held on and dismissed those reports.
  • There had been a slight improvement before the November international break, with the Hornets edging past Lincoln City before earning a creditable goalless draw against Middlesbrough.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Continuing to struggle down at the bottom end of the Championship table, Watford have now taken the decision to sack manager Alessio Dionisi.

Following a 5-1 defeat to Cardiff City last month, it was reported then that Dionisi was set to be sacked by Watford, but he held on and dismissed those reports.

There had been a slight improvement before the November international break, with the Hornets edging past Lincoln City before earning a creditable goalless draw against Middlesbrough.

However, they have returned from the break with a 4-0 shellacking at the hands of Sheffield United at Bramall Lane and that has prompted Dionisi to be let go of by The Hornets.

As a result, we have taken a look at five potential candidates to replace the former Empoli manager in Hertfordshire as Watford fight to keep their second-tier status.

Former Ecuador boss Sebastian Beccacece remains unemployed since leading the South Americans to the round of 32 of FIFA World Cup 2026, eventually losing to Mexico at Estadio Azteca in Mexico City.

According to recent reports, it had been a frustrating time in the group stages for the Ecuadoreans; unfortunately beaten 1-0 by Cote d’Ivoire in their opener before being held to a shock goalless draw by Curaçao. They did then manage to squeeze through with a dramatic victory over Germany at the MetLife Stadium in Latest York.

Unable to score due to a lack of quality was an glitch that plagued them throughout qualification, but a manager’s job is to get a team to create chances in attack and look organised at the back – two things Beccacece managed to do and impressively so in charge of Ecuador as they finished second in CONMEBOL qualification for the tournament, with just five goals conceded in their 18 qualifiers.

A lack of quality in the final third undermined the actual style of football that he had implemented and created with La Tri. He remains a highly-rated coach, and it would be an ambitious appointment for Watford to make but one that may be slightly more realistic after a frustrating summer for the Argentine.

Industry observers note that earlier this season, Parma parted company with manager Carlos Cuesta after a slow-ish start to the campaign. They have continued to struggle, though, and the lack of improvement, as shown by a 5-1 loss at home to Roma this weekend, only further speaks to the managerial qualities of Cuesta.

Cuesta, born in Majorca, began his professional coaching career as an assistant at Arsenal to Mikel Arteta from 2020 until the summer of 2025. He was poached by expected Serie A strugglers Parma at the age of just 29, turning 30 later in the month after his appointment.

In his debut season as a manager, and such a young one at that, Parma comfortably survived with an extremely impressive defensive record, perhaps to be expected by a duel-led, conservative-focused apprentice of Arteta.

Undermined by big-money defensive sales this summer, such as goalkeeper Zion Suzuki to Aston Villa and centre-back Alessandro Circati to Benfica, Parma were hasty in their decision to move on, fitting of being a Serie A club but a decision that they are perhaps already regretting and could open the door for Watford to find a real coup.

Without much of a playing career to discuss, Edward Iordanescu began his coaching as an assistant, and occasional caretaker, coach at Steaua Bucharest before going on to experience a bit of a journeyman career across Romania.

Iordanescu coached Fortuna Brazi and Targu Mures in 2013 before a couple of years in charge of Pandurii Targu Jiu and then short stints at CSKA Sofia, Astra Giurgiu, CFR Cluj and Gaz Metan Medias before returning to CFR Cluj for the 2020-21 campaign.

Recent findings suggest that having won the league title as well as a couple of Supercupa Romaniei with CFR Cluj, Iordanescu returned to FCSB, the artist formerly known as Steaua, before getting the Romania job in 2022. In charge of the national team, he led them to UEFA EURO 2024 qualification and even into the knockout stages of that competition before they were beaten 3-0 by the Netherlands in Munich.

His most recent job saw him take charge of Polish giants Legia Warsaw, but he was sacked in October of the same 2025-26 season after an average start to the campaign.

He was heavily linked with the job a few weeks ago and has held talks with the hierarchy, and so his name cropping again would be no surprise, despite his nomadic managerial career.

At the age of 65, it would certainly be a punt for Watford to give Jose Luis Mendilibar his first job in English football, but it would be a real coup for The Hornets should they choose to do so.

Old school in terms of his football values and general tactical philosophy, stereotypically Basque in that respect, Mendilibar has repeatedly got his teams to punch above their weight; be it taking Eibar into La Liga and making them a top-flight stalwart or leading Real Valladolid to a record points tally in the second-tier while reaching the quarter-finals of the Copa del Rey or performing a ‘great escape’ from La Liga relegation with Osasuna.

He was the firefighter brought in to keep fallen giants Sevilla from falling down to the second-tier after a poor stint in charge from Jorge Sampaoli; keeping the Andalusians up and also managing to win the UEFA Europa League, too.

He then took charge of Olympiacos and added a second European trophy to his cabinet with the Greek giants defeating Aston Villa in the semi-finals and Fiorentina in the final to win the UEFA Europa Conference League. Not able to sustain their best over a season eventually led to his dismissal, but title-challenging consistency is not required at Watford; grit, aggression and intensity it and Mendilibar provides that in abundance.

A slightly different style, but again, looking to Spain for an appointment could see Watford try and poach Almeria boss Garcia Pimienta.

Once one of the more highly-regarded young coaches in Spain, after beginning his coaching career at Barcelona B, Garcia Pimienta led Las Palmas to La Liga playing in a stereotypically Canarian manner, with Las Palmas often referred to as ‘the Brazilians of Spanish football’ and their passing style of football on their ascent was representative of that.

He was eventually poached from Las Palmas by Spanish giants Sevilla, but he was just one of many victims of Sevilla’s decline both on and off the pitch in recent years before rebuilding his reputation across Andalusia and at Almeria.

Pimienta took charge of an Almeria side that had lost the play-off final to regional rivals Malaga in the summer and have significant expectations to get back into La Liga and to kick on further than that with their spending.

In a recent development, who should Watford appoint as their newly introduced manager? Comment below!

So far this season, they have managed to collect 32 points from 14 matches, sitting five points clear of third place Granada but just a point behind league leaders Castellon, with Pimienta again showing his class and potential outside of the basket case of Seville, where even that now in hindsight looks like a reasonable job.

It has been revealed that once linked with Watford in 2025, could Pimienta now head to Vicarage Road? It wouldn't be a surprise if he was on Gino Pozzo's radar.

#129909. Transient contacts between filaments impart its elasticity to branched actin

Transient contacts between filaments impart its elasticity to branched actin

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1664 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Cells dynamically assemble actin into branched networks to push on their environment during cell migration, endocytosis or the maintenance of cell–cell contact1.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cells dynamically assemble actin into branched networks to push on their environment during cell migration, endocytosis or the maintenance of cell–cell contact1. These networks are among the stiffest found in the cytoskeleton and can generate large pushing stresses against stationary obstacles2,3,4,5. When grown against a controlled opposing stress in an atomic force microscope6 or inside the cell7, branched networks alter their own architecture to adapt their compressional stiffness to their environment, but the underpinnings of their mechanics and adaptability are unclear. Here we show that their high density and low connectivity place them outside the scope of standard elastic network models for actin. We show that they are instead dominated by the proliferation of interfilament contacts under compression. This places branched actin in the same category as undercoordinated fibrous materials such as sheep’s wool. When the network is grown under force, filaments entangle as if knitted together and trap contacts in their structure. Trapped contacts have a similar role as crosslinkers in rigidifying the network and are thus key to its active adaptive mechanics.

Latest footage highlights what Ryan Manning did during Southampton's 2nd goal v Derby County

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (513 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Southampton strolled to a comfortable 2-0 victory over Derby County at the weekend, but what Ryan Manning did in the build-up to the second goal ought to have Saints fans laughing.
  • Southampton have continued to climb the Championship table with their latest 2-0 home victory over struggling Derby at St Mary's on Saturday, courtesy of goals from Cyle Larin and Divin Mubama.
  • Despite Derby's insistence on disrupting Southampton's flow, the home side dominated large parts of the game and were deserving of the three points in the end, as Irish left-back Manning has certainly had the last laugh.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Southampton strolled to a comfortable 2-0 victory over Derby County at the weekend, but what Ryan Manning did in the build-up to the second goal ought to have Saints fans laughing.

Southampton have continued to climb the Championship table with their latest 2-0 home victory over struggling Derby at St Mary's on Saturday, courtesy of goals from Cyle Larin and Divin Mubama.

Despite Derby's insistence on disrupting Southampton's flow, the home side dominated large parts of the game and were deserving of the three points in the end, as Irish left-back Manning has certainly had the last laugh.

It took Southampton a while to really get going in their clash against Derby, with just one shot on target from either side in the first half, making it an extremely close encounter.

However, Eckert's half-time team talk appeared to have the effect the German would've been hoping for, as the Saints broke the deadlock with Larin just before the hour mark, before finally adding a second in the dying embers as Mubama raced through on goal to prod into an empty net following a Derby corner.

With Rams goalkeeper Jacob Widell Zetterström trying his luck in the penalty area in the closing stages, Mubama broke away after Lewis Dobbin played him through on goal, and running alongside the Manchester City loanee was Manning, who turned and appeared to laugh at the chasing Derby defenders.

The 30-year-old, who has developed into one of the best left-backs on the South Coast, has certainly endeared himself to the Southampton supporters since his arrival at the club in 2023, with this just being a fresh reminder of his character and importance to the side.

Manning's contract at St Mary's is due to expire in the summer, and as things stand, he's set to leave as a free agent in 2027.

However, he has made his intentions of staying at the club abundantly clear already, and having become a mainstay under Eckert, it would be a surprise if he wasn't offered fresh terms on the South Coast, regardless of whether a return to the Premier League is secured.

The Irishman will be free to speak to other clubs over a summer move in January, and with just over a month until the winter window, Southampton shouldn't leave this concern unresolved for much longer.

What have you made of Ryan Manning's time at Southampton? Would you like to see him offered a fresh deal? Share your thoughts below!

With Southampton climbing into the Championship play-off picture, Eckert will have set his sights firmly on the automatic promotion places right now.

If it weren't for their four-point deduction at the beginning of the campaign, the Saints would currently sit in 3rd place behind only Middlesbrough and Stoke City, level on points with Wolverhampton Wanderers but with a superior goal difference.

A return to the Premier League is certainly on the agenda in Hampshire, and Eckert will be looking to the likes of Manning to steer his side in the right direction over the course of the campaign.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AC Milan will hold their penultimate training session today in view of Sunday’s return to Serie A action with a game against Frosinone.

La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) writes that the Milan squad will return to full strength with the arrival of the final players returning from international duty, allowing Ruben Amorim to begin detailed preparations for Sunday’s 18:00 CET clash against Frosinone at San Siro.

Recent findings suggest that mike Maignan is expected to start in goal. He took part in a portion of yesterday’s training session alongside the other goalkeepers. The Frenchman’s recovery is progressing well, and Pietro Terracciano – who has been out for about 40 days with a shoulder issue – could make the bench.

Sources indicate that strahinja Pavlovic also participated in part of the group training and will be included in the squad for the match against the Ciociari. However, the Serbian defender is not yet at 100%, so unless his condition improves rapidly, he is likely to start on the bench.

Sankhoun Diawara would thus take the left centre-back spot, with either Davide Bartesaghi or Pervis Estupinan covering the left flank. The defence will be completed by Koni De Winter and Mario Gila, with the Spaniard operating on the right again.

In midfield, Yunus Musah, Luka Modric and Adrian Rabiot – who could play in a more advanced, attacking-midfield role – are expected to be the starting trio. In attack, Diego Moreira and Goncalo Ramos are guaranteed starters, with Christian Pulisic currently favoured over Alphadjo Cisse.

Predicted Milan XI (4-2-3-1): Maignan; Gila, De Winter, Diawara, Bartesaghi; Musah, Modric; Pulisic, Rabiot, Moreira; Ramos.

Predicted Frosinone XI (4-2-3-1): Palmisani; Oyono, Calvani, Monterisi, Terzic; Calo, Masini; Ghedjemis, Schmid, Kvernadze; Birligea.

Why Emile Heskey decided Bolton Wanderers would be his final club

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Former Premier League, Championship and England international forward, Emile Heskey, has revealed exactly why he opted to retire after a spell with Bolton Wanderers in the mid-2010s.
  • The 48-year-old turned out for some of English football's most historic clubs during a 22-year career, which included a high-profile switch from boyhood club, Leicester City, to Liverpool for £11m in the year 2000.
  • Heskey accumulated 62 England caps and netted seven goals during his esteemed career, as well as winning eight major honours.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Former Premier League, Championship and England international forward, Emile Heskey, has revealed exactly why he opted to retire after a spell with Bolton Wanderers in the mid-2010s.

The 48-year-old turned out for some of English football's most historic clubs during a 22-year career, which included a high-profile switch from boyhood club, Leicester City, to Liverpool for £11m in the year 2000.

Heskey accumulated 62 England caps and netted seven goals during his esteemed career, as well as winning eight major honours.

Having racked up 516 appearances in the Premier League alongside 110 goals and 49 assists, Heskey then returned to Championship level for the first time in 18 years in December 2014 when he initially signed a short-term contract at the Toughsheet Community Stadium.

After leaving Liverpool in 2004, Heskey went on to feature for Birmingham City, Wigan Athletic and Aston Villa, as well as a two-season spell with Newcastle Jets of the Australian A-League between 2012 and 2014.

Returning to England in late 2014, it was confirmed the striker would sign an initial short-term contract with the Whites, who were managed by Heskey's former Leicester teammate, Neil Lennon, at the time.

During his final career stint, he was partnered with Icelandic striker, Eidur Gudjohnsen, who had returned to the North West for a second spell earlier in December 2014, with the latter providing a debut goal for Heskey against Blackburn Rovers on Boxing Day of 2014.

In total, Heskey made 48 appearances for Wanderers, but his only full season at the club and the last of his career ended in relegation to League One, before he became one of 13 players who departed upon the expiration of their contracts.

Heskey started just 15 Championship games in his final career season, scoring twice against Charlton Athletic and Brighton and Hove Albion, but had already surpassed his 38th birthday at the midpoint of the campaign.

There are several examples of one-time top-level strikers continuing to lead the line into their 40s, but speaking to current Burnley forward, Jamie Vardy, Heskey revealed how he knew it was time for him to call it quits on his playing days.

"I went to Australia for two years then came back to Bolton," he remarked.

"It was basically, in training, more or less, when you see young kids running past you, and you think, not 'I can't do this anymore', because I could've, and I was in good shape and I felt fine, but I didn't want people running past me and not being able to tackle and get back at them like my head was telling me I could do.

"I was like, 'Do I really want to keep going down the leagues to League One and League Two and continue there', just for what?," Heskey admitted.

Bolton fans, did Emile Heskey still impress you in his career's latter stages? Comment below!

Recent findings suggest that "My boys were getting bigger, and I just decided that was enough for me. I got to 38 and probably could've played another one or two years, I think.".

Vardy, 39, is known for his remarkable 200-goal exploits at Leicester, during which he won the Premier League, FA Cup, Community Shield and two Championship titles between 2012 and 2025.

However, he then admitted to Heskey that he has had similar conversations with ex-professionals who may have retired earlier in their 30s, with the Sheffield native still turning out on a regular basis in the second tier.

There are shades between the final club stint of Heskey's career and his own, with Burnley at the moment in a dire predicament in the Championship after relegation from the Premier League, as they could emulate the unwanted feats of Luton Town and Leicester and become the third team to suffer successive relegations from the top-flight to League One in as many years.

He scored goals for QPR and Nottingham Forest - Then tried to transform healthcare

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (950 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Life after professional football has been a mixed bag for Dexter Blackstock, but the former striker has found himself a upcoming niche in the pharmaceutical industry.
  • According to recent reports, upon first glance, the post-playing career options of the professional footballer can appear somewhat limited.
  • But by the time that most players reach their late twenties, there may be decisions that have to be made, and in the case of Dexter Blackstock, a player who built himself a fearsome reputation as a striker with a number of clubs including Nottingham Forest and Queens Park Rangers, the decisions that he did make coupled with his entrepreneurial instincts have led him into an industry that few would have expected while he was playing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Life after professional football has been a mixed bag for Dexter Blackstock, but the former striker has found himself a upcoming niche in the pharmaceutical industry.

According to recent reports, upon first glance, the post-playing career options of the professional footballer can appear somewhat limited. Coaching or the media are the obvious options, but paid employment in these sectors can be limited, and it might not appeal to all.

But by the time that most players reach their late twenties, there may be decisions that have to be made, and in the case of Dexter Blackstock, a player who built himself a fearsome reputation as a striker with a number of clubs including Nottingham Forest and Queens Park Rangers, the decisions that he did make coupled with his entrepreneurial instincts have led him into an industry that few would have expected while he was playing.

Born in Oxford and brought up in Oxford United's youth academy, Dexter Blackstock had his first breakthrough in the senior game after transferring to Southampton in 2003. First brought into the first-team squad during an injury crisis, he came off the bench at half-time during a League Cup match in September 2004 against Colchester United with the Saints trailling by a goal to nil, scoring a second half hat-trick to help secure the Saints a 3-2 win.

Despite this - and scoring in a hotly-contested Premier League derby match with Portsmouth a couple of months later - Blackstock was unable to tie down a regular starting place in the Southampton team and, following spells on loan with Plymouth Argyle and Derby County, moved on to Queens Park Rangers in 2006.

Blackstock would go on to build his reputation further at Loftus Road, scoring 32 times in 117 appearances for QPR over the next three years. He also made two appearances for the England under-21s during this time, having also played for the under-18 and under-19 teams while at Southampton.

But in March 2009, he was sent on loan to a Nottingham Forest team that was battling to avoid relegation from the Championship, amid reports that he would be going to The City Ground permanently should they stay up. Forest ended the season in 19th place in the table, and consequently his move was made permanent that summer.

Blackstock spent seven years at Forest, with a loan spell at Leeds United in 2013. He had some problems with injuries while he was there, missing a year from November 2010 with a knee ligament injury, but still managed to score 44 goals for them in 187 appearances. And while he never got to play a full international match for England, he did also qualify to play for Antigua & Barbuda and made 12 appearances for them between 2012 and 2016.

He left Nottingham Forest by mutual consent at the end of the summer 2016 transfer window and moved on to Rotherham United, but his spell with the Millers only lasted a year before his three-year contract was mutually cancelled after a year, and he retired from the game at 31 years of age.

By the time that his playing career came to an end, Blackstock already had an idea of what he wanted to do afterwards. He'd built up a portfolio of buy-to-let properties, but his early experience as a landlord wasn't successful.

Industry observers note that in October 2019, he was fined £24,000 at Nottingham Magistrates Court after inspectors found a number of his properties to be in a state of disrepair. He admitted 12 counts of failing to license the properties and was fined £24,000 and ordered to pay £1,100 costs and a £170 victim surcharge on top of his fine. In 2021, he was ordered to repay £8,500 in housing benefit that he'd received for the unlicensed properties.

Recent findings suggest that but Blackstock's entrpreneurial leanings had by this time already taken him in a newly introduced direction. He formed MediConnect with a view towards using blockchain technology to counter the negative image that online pharmacies had received over concerns regarding a lack of controls to prevent the over-prescription of strong painkillers to customers.

According to recent reports, at the start of 2019, Blackstock spoke to The Sun about his new business venture, and also shone a little light on the end of his playing career. “I had lost my mojo and I had no intention of carrying on playing football", he told them, "I wasn’t enjoying playing at Rotherham." On his move into pharmaceuticals, he added, "As it stands, there is nothing to stop anyone ordering drugs from one online pharmacy, then exactly the same with another tech giant and then going down to their local GP and topping up with the same.".

In 2021, Blackstock spoke to World Pharmaceutical Frontiers in greater detail about his vision. "Anyone who’s using an online pharmacy platform will need a unique customer number and every transaction will be put on the blockchain," he told them, "so the next pharmacy can check whether the patient can have that drug in the same timeframe or mix the drugs.".

Sources indicate that the previous year, at the height of the Covid-19 pandemic, he told the BBC that he was using his company to help the public donate personal protective equipment (PPE) to frontline staff dealing with the pandemic. By 2023, he had a reported net worth of £7.8 million, with The Sun reporting that, "the bulk of his earnings" was still coming "from the 50 properties he owns." If nothing else, the experience of Dexter Blackstock demonstrates that the post-career options for the professional footballer are as broad as their imaginations will let them believe.

It has been revealed that the 54-year-old has built a close working relationship with his coaching team throughout spells at Espanyol, Southampton, Tottenham, Paris Saint-Germain and Chelsea. Several of those staff members have followed him to Manchester United.

The former Argentine defender has worked with Pochettino since his first managerial job at Espanyol. He has been involved in training sessions, video analysis and tactical preparation, helping the manager develop game aims.

Is Mauricio Pochettino’s job at Manchester United the toughest in the Premier League?

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (515 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Readmanutd

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Manchester United hired Mauricio Pochettino as their next manager to replace Michael Carrick, who managed just one win in 10 games.
  • His appointment makes him Manchester United’s eighth permanent manager since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013.
  • In a recent development, pochettino brings considerable Premier League experience after previous spells with Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United hired Mauricio Pochettino as their next manager to replace Michael Carrick, who managed just one win in 10 games.

His appointment makes him Manchester United’s eighth permanent manager since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013.

In a recent development, pochettino brings considerable Premier League experience after previous spells with Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea. He has also managed Paris Saint-Germain before the USA job.

As he faces Liverpool for his first game on Sunday, the question arises: is he facing the toughest job in the Premier League?

The question was posed on BBC Radio about who is going to have more pressure, Pochettino or Thomas Frank at Crystal Palace.

According to former Premier League defender Nedum Onuoha, the expectations surrounding Manchester United will make the Argentine’s job considerably harder.

Industry observers note that pochettino is preparing for his first game in charge of Manchester United, with Liverpool waiting at Anfield on November 22. However, the challenge facing the newly introduced manager goes beyond getting results on the pitch.

Onuoha believes Pochettino will have to deal with constant discussion and criticism about his work, much of it coming from former United players who are now in the media.

Choosing between Pochettino and Frank, Onuoha noted, “Probably Pochettino, because every former Manchester United player works in the media, so there will always be discussion around what he is doing.

“Whereas Frank can just enjoy playing his football at Crystal Palace. If he does well then it is great, if he doesn’t do well then it is still OK.

“But from Pochettino’s perspective, if Manchester United finish the season 15th in the Premier League, whether we like it or not, there will be some criticism of him because he’s had 28 games to do something.”.

The comments just highlight the difference in expectations at the two clubs. Frank may have more freedom to work without the same level of attention, while Pochettino will be judged from day one against the standards historically associated with Manchester United. That is one significant problem for Pochettino.

In a recent development, rory Smith from The Observer highlighted another glaring problem at United. Highlighting a major problem, Smith noted, “there is a cycle element to Manchester United whereby a manager comes in, makes things a bit better, and then within a year to 18 months they aren’t challenging for titles again because the Premier League has changed since they were a dominant force.”.

Industry observers note that pochettino’s first taste of action as a United manager will be against Liverpool at Anfield on November 22. That opening fixture will give him an immediate test, but the bigger task will be to get back United to winning ways, step by step.

Industry observers note that will the Manchester United job be without pressure for Mauricio Pochettino? Absolutely Not.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United are prepared to consider legal action if evidence emerges that another club approached academy forward JJ Gabriel without permission.

The 16-year-old confirmed his departure from Old Trafford in a social media video on Tuesday and is expected to join Real Madrid in January. According to The Times and ESPN, United remain concerned about the circumstances surrounding his proposed move, although no breach of transfer regulations has been established.

Gabriel has been absent from United since September, when he requested the cancellation of his registration. The teenager remains registered with the club, and United could explore legal or regulatory options if evidence of an unauthorised approach emerges.

The Independent reports that United do not want to punish Gabriel for actions they believe may have been taken by adults involved in his future. Real Madrid have been widely linked with the forward, but his transfer has not been formally completed.

Gabriel joined United’s academy in 2020 and was named the club’s young player of the year last season. He featured for the senior side during pre-season but has not made a competitive first-team appearance.

The youngster is eligible for a move within the European Union under an exception to FIFA’s rules on international transfers involving players aged under 18. In his farewell message, Gabriel thanked United for helping him develop during his six years at the club.

In a recent development, his expected move to Madrid would bring that association to an end, although questions remain over the process leading to his departure. United have not unveiled legal proceedings, and there has been no finding of wrongdoing by Real Madrid or any other club.

He was a Coventry City and Aston Villa goal machine - Then invented something unusual

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Dion Dublin is one of English football's most well-respected former professionals, with the 57-year-old's playing and post-playing career certainly generating plenty of interest.

The Leicester native plied his trade for some of the country's most historic clubs at various levels, including a spell in the Championship with Norwich City towards the very end of his career.

Such is his current presence, it is fair to say that those of various generations will know Dublin either for his goalscoring exploits in the 1990s and 2000s, or either as a television personality, having followed in the footsteps of various other high-profile names within the game,.

However, it is fair to say that not everyone will be familiar with the former striker's attempts to forge a career in the music industry, which made headlines just over a decade ago.

Dublin was well-travelled throughout his career, with a breakthrough spell at Cambridge United eventually paving the way for his success as a Premier League-level striker.

The Yellows climbed two divisions during the forward's time at the club between 1990 and 1992, during which he netted the first play-off final-winning strike at Wembley against Chesterfield, before being sold to Manchester United for £1m.

Dublin's Old Trafford spell has been well-documented due to a serious leg injury which pushed him below the likes of Eric Cantona in Sir Alex Ferguson's pecking order, and after two years, the striker joined Coventry City for £2m.

His goalscoring touch was then reignited at Highfield Road, netting 72 times in 162 appearances, including an 18-goal campaign in 1997/98 in which he ended as the Premier League's joint-highest scorer alongside Chris Sutton and Michael Owen.

Dublin then spent just under six years at Aston Villa under John Gregory, Graham Taylor and David O'Leary, scoring 59 times in 192 games, as well as infamously being sent off in a Second City derby defeat to Birmingham City in 2003 for headbutting Robbie Savage.

During the latter stages of his Villa spell, Dublin went on to feature in what is now the Championship on loan with Millwall in 2001/02, as the Lions made the play-offs but were defeated in agonising fashion by Birmingham at the semi-final stage.

After leaving B6 in 2004, the experienced figure moved to his hometown club, Leicester City, for two seasons, scoring six times in 42 appearances in the 2004/05 season, before featuring just 21 times the following season.

A spell with Celtic sandwiched his time at the King Power Stadium and a return to academy side, Norwich City, for two seasons where Dublin wound down his playing days between 2006 and 2008, scoring 16 times in 79 appearances, despite occasionally being drafted in to feature as a centre-back.

Dublin then became a regular fixture on television screens post-retirement, but as well as this, rediscovered his love for music, which led to an intriguing creation.

In 2013, it was revealed that the former striker had invented the 'dube' - described as a "cube-based drum played with the hands.".

This led to concerts with the People's Orchestra, which revealed just how much this side of his life helped Dublin through the aforementioned difficult six-month injury setback with the Red Devils.

Did you know about Dion Dublin's musical invention? Comment below!

"Not having had the opportunity to play with a full orchestra before I am excited to be taking the Dube, the percussion drum I invented seven years ago, with me to perform on the day," he remarked.

Whilst Dublin's music invention is certainly lesser-known, what isn't is that the four-time England international has been a regular daytime television presenter on BBC One's 'Homes Under the Hammer'.

It was, rather unsurprisingly, baffling to many of the show's audience when the decision was made in 2015 for Dublin to join Martin Roberts and Lucy Alexander on the show, as well as his punditry roles on BBC Sport.

During his 11 years on the show, Dublin has become infamous for his line of "stairs leading up to the bedroom," but revealed that this sector is another of his great passions.

"I have a passion for property and look forward to meeting people on the show who share that passion," he said when landing this particular long-standing gig.

Breaking: Designing dislocation-driven polar vortex networks in twisted perovskites

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 15 min read (3025 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~15 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, twisting two atomic layers produces a geometric moiré pattern but bonding-induced interfacial reconstruction fundamentally transforms this into an ordered dislocation network—a distinction obscured in weakly bonded van der Waals systems.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, twisting two atomic layers produces a geometric moiré pattern but bonding-induced interfacial reconstruction fundamentally transforms this into an ordered dislocation network—a distinction obscured in weakly bonded van der Waals systems. Although in-plane topological vortex nanostructures arising from twisting-induced lateral strain modulation have been linked to periodic moiré patterns in freestanding perovskite layers1,2,3 and 2D bilayers4, their coupling to the interfacial dislocation network in twisted layers remains unresolved. Here we demonstrate that twisted freestanding SrTiO3 (STO) layers undergo interfacial reconstruction into a network of screw dislocations, accompanied by the emergence of in-plane topological vortices. Unlike in previous reports, these vortices are associated with the dislocation network rather than with geometric moiré patterns. Four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4DSTEM) reveals a beam deflection texture in registry with the interfacial dislocation network. A machine learning interatomic potential, trained on first-principles calculations, together with phase-field modelling, confirms that competing strains within the dislocation network stabilize polar vortex–antivortex pairs; first-principles calculations further reveal the emergence of an electronic superlattice with a well-defined periodicity. Our results establish twist-controlled dislocation networks as a latest and versatile route to designing local polar and electronic structures in oxide materials.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Manchester United signed Lisandro Martinez in 2022 from Ajax for £57 million but at the end of his contract, he might leave United for free.
  • Sources indicate that martinez is now in his fifth season at Old Trafford after joining from Ajax for £57 million in 2022.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United signed Lisandro Martinez in 2022 from Ajax for £57 million but at the end of his contract, he might leave United for free.

Sources indicate that martinez is now in his fifth season at Old Trafford after joining from Ajax for £57 million in 2022. He has made 121 appearances in all competitions for the club, but his long-term future remains unclear.

Manchester United are not expected to stand in his way if a suitable opportunity to leave comes, especially following his public criticism of the club’s transfer strategy last month.

The defender is out of contract at the end of the season, although United have the option to trigger a further 12 months. Whether the club chooses to use that clause remains to be seen.

Industry observers note that A departure from Manchester United could give Martinez the chance to find a latest challenge after four seasons in Manchester. Barcelona had looked like a possible destination, but the latest reports suggest they are not right now pushing for his signature.

Lisandro Martinez’s hopes of joining Barcelona appear to have suffered a major setback, with reports from Spain claiming that neither sporting director Deco nor manager Hansi Flick is convinced by the Manchester United defender.

Atletico Madrid had also been mentioned among the interested clubs but there weren’t any further reports on a possible transfer, leaving Martínez’s options in Spain uncertain.

The latest claims suggest a switch to the Camp Nou may be unlikely.

Journalist Pedro Bravo on El Chiringuito reports that Martínez’s profile does not appeal to either member of Barcelona’s sporting leadership.

“Lisandro, as far as I’m aware, neither Deco nor Flick are keen on him,” Bravo was quoted as saying.

The journalist also claimed to have spoken directly with Deco, who is also ruled Martinez out.

“He’s a good player, but we don’t like him. He doesn’t fit in with us.”.

❌ "LISANDRO MARTÍNEZ NO GUSTA a DECO ni FLICK".😱 El superagente @PedroBravoJ lo desvela en #ElChiringuitoEnEnergy. pic.twitter.com/Frt2KAG3q4.

In a recent development, lisandro Martinez is not expected to renew his current contract but would be expecting that United doesn’t trigger his one-year extension clause. With United not expected to sell him in the winter transfer window, United may be looking at extending his deal to recoup some transfer fees by selling him in the summer transfer window.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Former Premier League star and Serbian international Sasa Curcic earned both fame in his home country and a substantial payout after becoming a reality TV star following his retirement from the game.

Industry observers note that as professional footballers reach the end of their playing careers, many are left with difficult decisions over what to do with their futures. Even the luckiest of players only make it until their mid-to-late thirties in the professional game, and the question of what to do after playing contracts dry up is a very real one.

Industry observers note that for some, coaching or scouting is an option, while for others there is a clear appeal to a post-playing career in the media. By taking these routes, former players can rely on the experience that they picked up over the decades during which they were involved in the game. Others enter into business, being able to invest as a result of their time in the game.

But for some players, what's missing is the roar of the crowd, and in the case of the former Aston Villa, Bolton Wanderers and Crystal Palace star Sasa Curcic, the former player found a whole fresh audience as a reality TV star once his playing days were over.

Industry observers note that sasa Curcic arrived in England having already impressed in his home city of Belgrade. Having first signed for OFK Beograd in 1991, he moved to Partizan Belgrade two years later, having already made his debut for the FR Yugoslavia — now Serbia & Montenegro — national team at the very start of his professional career.

In the summer of 1995, Bolton Wanderers had just been promoted to the Premier League and were looking to strengthen. Curcic was an obvious talent, so was signed by Bolton’s managerial team of Colin Todd and Roy McFarland as they sought to avoid a quick return to the second-tier.

Recent findings suggest that what are your memories of Sasa Curcic? Let us know in the comments below!

Described by When Saturday Comes as "the greatest thriller at Burnden Park since the iconic Frank Worthington", Curcic was given a free role in the Bolton midfield, but he was unable to keep his team in the Premier League; they were relegated back in bottom place in the table.

But having tasted life in the Premier League with Bolton, Curcic wanted to stay there following the club's relegation, and at the start of the 1996-97 season he left for Aston Villa. It was a disastrous move. Curcic fell out with manager Brian Little, and he left the club in March 1998 for Crystal Palace with just 29 League appearances under his belt. The move from Bolton to Villa was later ranked by The Times as the 12th-worst in the first ten years of the Premier League.

But life at Selhurst Park proved to be no easier for him. He managed just 23 League appearances for Palace before leaving the club in 1999, with his spell in South London best-remembered for his protests against NATO bombing of Serbia while he was playing for Palace. After spells in Major League Soccer and in Scotland with Motherwell, he confirmed his retirement as a player in 2001.

Having picked up a total of 14 appearances for his national team, Curcic was still well-known in Serbia, and he capitalised on that when he entered the Celebrity Big Brother house for their version of the show in May 2007.

As one of thirteen contestants, Curcic proved that he was still able to get people on his side, and it was confirmed a month later that he'd won the competition, scooping a prize of €50,000 and earning himself some lucrative television commercial work as a result of it.

But fame wouldn't last for him. He left the set of another reality show called Farma — "The Farm" — after just a couple of weeks the following year and faded from view again, eventually resurfacing back in South London in 2015, forming an academy with connections to Crystal Palace. He also had a spell managing, back in his home country. Appointed into the head coach's position at the Belgrade-based club Borac Lazarevac in November 2021, he lasted six months in the position before leaving.

Recent findings suggest that always a bit of a wild child — Brian Little would later tell a few stories of the midfielder's eccentricities, including "hiring a double-decker booze bus with models for his Aston Villa teammates" — Curcic himself later admitted that moving to England in the first place had been a bit of a mistake: "My dream was to play for Partizan, my team. I should have stayed. I would have my own stand, I’d be manager.".

It speaks volumes for the self-confidence that got him to the top of the game in England and his subsequent fall from grace that he continued to believe in the certainty that his career would have ended up so differently had he stayed in Serbia in the first place. And Bolton Wanderers fans of a certain age certainly still remember the role he played following their original return to the Premier League.

Mauricio Pochettino’s first Manchester United training session was secretly filmed by a drone operator, who has since apologised and removed the footage from his YouTube channel after admitting his actions were unethical.

Sources indicate that around 12 minutes of footage from Carrington was recorded on Thursday and uploaded to a YouTube channel. The video offered supporters an early glimpse of Mauricio Pochettino working with his fresh squad, but its release swiftly raised concerns about the privacy of United’s training sessions.

The footage highlighted players split into smaller groups carrying out different drills. On a separate full-size pitch, 11 players were positioned across the field alongside mannequins before gathering to receive instructions and feedback from new head coach Mauricio Pochettino.

After backlash from fans over the breach of privacy, the video was removed on Friday morning, with the operator issuing an apology for filming the session.

In his statement, the operator said the flight itself was legal under drone regulations but accepted that recording the training session was wrong.

He explained that his intention was to give Manchester United supporters their first look at Pochettino wearing the club’s training kit.

He said: “A total error of judgement on my part led to me filming some of the Manchester United training session at Carrington, whilst the flight was legal in terms of drone laws I fully accept it was unethical on my part.”.

The operator apologized directly to the club, its upcoming head coach and the players.

“I would like to apologise to Manchester United, Mauricio Pochettino and the players for my actions and sincerely hope those actions do not affect the outcome of any match.”.

“The video has been removed from my channel,” he added.

Writing in The Telegraph, the former Liverpool defender highlighted the irony of United turning to a manager whose own career needs a fresh start.

Sources indicate that “Manchester United need a savior to first ease them from the relegation zone and then revive their Premier League and Champions League credibility. Pochettino, meanwhile, needed a club like United to save him from a managerial career that promised more than it delivered.”.

“The South American returns to England with a big reputation, but not enough on his CV to back up glowing testimonials,” he continued.

Carrick believes one of the biggest concerns surrounding Pochettino is his record in key matches.

“A recurring issue with Pochettino, which continued with the US team, is an inability to get over the line in the most consequential, winnable matches, resulting in a lack of substantial trophies.”.

Despite questioning his ability to bottle in substantial games, he praised his teams when everything comes in together.

Recent findings suggest that “Ten years ago his best team were the embodiment of him, full of energy, style and ambition. Time will tell whether this version of Pochettino is the one turning up at Old Trafford.”.

Pochettino will have the chance to shut Carragher’s doubts on Sunday when Manchester United face Liverpool. His immediate priority will be to take United out of the relegation zone, but the expectations at Old Trafford will extend far beyond survival.

According to recent reports, the Liverpool fixture will be his first opportunity to make an impression. Carragher, however, believes the Argentine’s real challenge is to turn his reputation into success.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The former Plymouth, Bristol Rovers and Wycombe Wanderers forward is in trouble with the law, and this is far from the first time that this has happened.
  • The former EFL forward Chris Zebroski is back in trouble with the law again.
  • Zebroski had been appointed as a player-coach at Southern League side Gosport Borough during the summer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The former Plymouth, Bristol Rovers and Wycombe Wanderers forward is in trouble with the law, and this is far from the first time that this has happened.

The former EFL forward Chris Zebroski is back in trouble with the law again. Appearing at Swindon Magistrates' Court on the 7th October, Zebroski pleaded guilty to assault causing actual bodily harm following an incident which was described as an "alcohol-fuelled attack" in which "the 39-year-old headbutted the older man and knocked out one of his teeth, leaving him with a significant purple bruise under his eye.".

Zebroski had been appointed as a player-coach at Southern League side Gosport Borough during the summer.

Chris Zebroski started his career at Swindon Town, but moved to Plymouth Argyle after failing to be offered a senior contract at The County Ground, following a spell with non-league Cirencester City. But he first hit the headlines for all the wrong reasons in August 2007 after he was sacked by the club for gross misconduct following an altercation in the bar during their pre-season tour of Austria the previous month, which left the club captain Paul Wotton with cuts to his head.

Zebroski moved on to Millwall and then to Wycombe Wanderers, but his legal problems continued to pile up. After going on loan to Torquay United, where he was a success in his first season with 19 goals for them in the National League throughout the 2007-08 season, he was given a 12-month community order and a fine for kicking and punching a soldier in a street fight in Torquay in August 2010.

What are your memories of Chris Zebroski as a player? Let us know in the comments below!

He left Wycombe in 2011 to return to Torquay before moving on to Bristol Rovers, After one unsuccessful season there, he joined Cheltenham Town, but midway through his first season at Whaddon Road he had his contract cancelled after repeatedly pulling out of the first-team squad at short notice.

His next move was into the non-league game with Eastleigh, but at the end of the 2012-13 season he was picked up by Newport County. Again, he was a success on the pitch, with 12 goals in 35 League Two appearances as the Exiles finished 14th in League Two, but again his extracurricular activities would come to catch up with him.

Sources indicate that the law would come to catch up with Zebroski again in the summer of 2015, and this time the matter at hand was far more serious. His second season at Rodney Parade had been less successful than his first, with seven goals scored in 36 appearances, but he found himself back in court in July 2015, pleading guilty to four charges of robbery, attempted robbery and assault in relation to two incidents.

The first of these incidents had come in December 2014, when Zebroski crashed his BMW into a taxi and then attacked a witness - another taxi driver - who filmed him when he got out of the car, trying to take his mobile phone from him.

Industry observers note that the BBC reported at the time that: "Zebroski hit Mr Madhu [one of the taxi drivers] in the side of the head and tried to wrestle his mobile phone from him before taking and smashing it. Mr Vladimirej [the other taxi driver] ran off so Zebroski chased him, pushed him to the ground and punched him at least 10 times, saying "give me your phone."" He was also found to have assaulted and attempted to rob two men the following February.

Sources indicate that in mitigation, Zebroski's counsel pleaded that his client had an alcohol problem, but neither the court nor his employers were impressed by this explanation. He was sentenced to four years and four months in prison, and had his contract terminated by Newport County.

It has been revealed that he was released after serving two years of his prison sentence, and later claimed that he had come close to re-signing for Newport County after leaving prison. At the time, Zebroski said that, "To get sent to jail had a big impact, a massive wake-up call," and that, "Playing in jail, it definitely built my character.".

This time there were no further offers from EFL clubs, and Zebroski instead ended up as a non-league journeyman, playing for numerous clubs before arriving at Gosport in the summer as a player/coach, and on the pitch, this hasn't been a bad season for Gosport, who are mid-table in the Southern League Premier Division South.

Industry observers note that but it's been a different matter behind the scenes. Manager Simon Lane was sacked just two games into the season, but his replacement, Jermaine McGlashan, left the club for personal reasons on the 7th October, meaning that they're already onto their third manager of the season. Whether it's a coincidence or not that McGlashan left Gosport on the same day that Zebroski pleaded guilty to the latest set of charges brought against him is unknown.

What is clear about Chris Zebroski's story is that he has been given plenty of chances. After the incidents at Plymouth, Torquay, Cheltenham and Newport, he managed to find someone who would take him on again, but whether this will be the case should he be sentenced to time in prison again is unknown. Zebroski passed forty years of age at the end of October 2026, and his contract position with Gosport will remain unclear until the cost of his latest loss of control is confirmed.

Sources indicate that fans of the clubs for whom he played may well be left wondering what he could have been capable of had he been able to stay on the right side of the law throughout his playing career. And any chances of launching a successful coaching career may already have been blighted by his latest legal problems.

Given that there have been almost two decades since getting sacked by Plymouth and his current predicament during which he might have successfully tackled the underlying issues which lead to these outbreaks of violence, it doesn't seem especially likely that he'll be given many more opportunities within the game.

Manchester United could welcome back Patrick Dorgu and Harry Maguire after both trained following fitness concerns. They were seen in that leaked drone footage as well. Lisandro Martínez is also available again after serving his suspension.

It has been revealed that luke Shaw and Marcus Rashford could return, although their availability remains uncertain. Carlos Baleba, Manuel Ugarte and Benjamin Sesko are still sidelined.

The latest United boss has a difficult personal record against Liverpool. Pochettino has faced the Reds 19 times, winning three, drawing five and losing 11. He has also failed to win any of his last eight meetings with them in all competitions. That might be a concern, but everything has a first time.

Recent findings suggest that pochettino will be encouraged by United’s overall record against Liverpool. United have an edge with 85 wins compared to Liverpool’s 72 across 218 meetings. Their most recent encounter also went their way, with a 3-2 victory on May 3.

However, United arrive on a disappointing run of seven consecutive away matches without a win and have managed just one victory in their last 11 games.
